To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PI and DAPI are suitable nuclear stains for subgross breast pathology, with PI being the best choice for BABB clearing; PI and EB are suitable stains for whole mount breast pathology, with EB being the best choice; PI is suitable for subgross breast immunohistochemistry, with BABB being the best choice of clearing agent; and thiodiglycols are not suitable for clearing breast tissue.

(a) alum-carmine and haematoxylins provide excellent subgross staining of thick sections of breast tissue; (b) DAPI and EB penetrate poorly, but PI penetrates thick sections well, with a good signal-to-noise; (c) BABB and xylene-BABB are effective clearing agents for PI, but thiodiglycoal is not, and (d) PI staining is compatible with IHC for ER and other markers.
PI staining and BABB clearing are a promising combination for subgross breast pathology.
